title: Evaporative Emission Control System
plain: The EVAP system traps gasoline vapors from the fuel tank so they do not escape into the air. The computer found a general problem with that system, such as a leak or a valve not working.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives
Faint fuel smell in some cases

causes.name: Loose, damaged or wrong gas cap
Leaking EVAP hose or charcoal canister

checks: Check that the gas cap clicks tight and its seal is not cracked
Have a smoke test done to find leaks
Test the purge and vent valves with a scan tool
fix: Often a gas cap, purge valve or vent valve; a smoke test pinpoints leaks.

cost.job: Smoke test and repair EVAP leak

drive: Usually safe to keep driving; this is an emissions-system fault that rarely changes how the car runs. Make sure the gas cap is on tight. If you smell strong raw fuel or see fuel leaking, stop driving and get it checked right away because of the fire risk.
test_first: Check the gas cap seal first, then smoke test the EVAP system and command the purge and vent valves before replacing the canister or valves.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Incorrect Purge Flow
plain: The purge valve lets stored fuel vapors get burned in the engine. The computer sees vapor flow when there should be none, or no flow when there should be some.
symptoms: Rough idle or hard starting right after refueling if the purge valve sticks open
Usually no change in driving otherwise

causes.name: Faulty purge valve (stuck open or closed)
Wiring fault at the purge valve

checks: Check the purge valve holds vacuum when off and opens when commanded
Inspect purge hoses between the engine and canister
Look for charcoal granules in the purge lines
fix: Usually a new purge valve; sometimes a hose or charcoal canister.
drive: Usually safe to keep driving. If the car is hard to start or stalls right after refueling, get it checked sooner, since a stall in traffic is risky. If you smell strong raw fuel or see a leak, stop and get it looked at.
test_first: Command the purge valve with a scan tool and check that it seals when off and flows when on, inspect the purge hose and canister, and check the tank pressure sensor before replacing parts.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (small leak)
plain: The computer found a small leak in the system that stores fuel vapors, about the size of a pinhole. It is not dangerous but it does let fuel vapor escape.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Gas cap seal worn or not tightened
Cracked EVAP hose or loose fitting

checks: Tighten or replace the gas cap and clear the code
Have a smoke test done to find the leak
Inspect hoses near the tank and canister
fix: Often a gas cap or small hose; a smoke test finds the exact leak.

cost.job: Smoke test and repair EVAP leak

drive: Usually safe to keep driving; this is an emissions-system fault that rarely changes how the car runs. Make sure the gas cap is on tight. If you smell strong raw fuel or see fuel leaking, stop driving and get it checked right away because of the fire risk.
test_first: Inspect and test the gas cap, then smoke test the EVAP system to find the leak before replacing the canister, valves or hoses.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Purge Control Valve Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem with the purge valve, the part that lets stored fuel vapors be drawn into the engine.
symptoms: Possible rough idle or hard start after refueling

causes.name: Damaged connector at the purge valve

checks: Measure the purge valve resistance
Check for power at the purge valve connector with the key on
Inspect wiring near hot engine parts
fix: Usually a new purge valve or a wiring repair.
drive: Usually safe to keep driving. If the engine idles rough or is hard to start after refueling, get it checked sooner. If you smell strong raw fuel or see a leak, stop and get it looked at.
test_first: Check the fuse, connector and wiring to the purge valve, measure the solenoid's resistance, and confirm the computer's command before replacing the valve or computer.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Purge Control Valve Circuit Open
plain: The computer sees a break in the electrical circuit for the EVAP purge valve.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives
checks: Check the purge valve connector and resistance
Check for power at the connector
fix: Usually a new purge valve or a wiring repair.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Purge Control Valve Circuit Shorted
plain: The computer sees a short in the electrical circuit for the EVAP purge valve.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Wiring shorted to ground or power

checks: Measure the purge valve resistance against spec
Inspect wiring for chafing
fix: Usually a new purge valve or a wiring repair.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Vent Control Circuit
plain: The vent valve lets fresh air in and out of the charcoal canister and closes during leak tests. The computer sees a problem with that valve or its circuit.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives
Possible trouble filling the tank (pump nozzle clicks off)

causes.name: Vent valve or filter clogged with dirt, water or bugs
Damaged wiring or connector at the vent valve

checks: Inspect the vent valve and filter near the tank for dirt or spider webs
Command the vent valve closed and open with a scan tool
Check power and ground at the valve connector
fix: Usually a new vent valve; sometimes a charcoal canister or wiring repair.
drive: Usually safe to keep driving. If the pump nozzle keeps clicking off, don't force extra fuel in. If you smell strong raw fuel or see fuel leaking, stop driving and get it checked right away because of the fire risk.
test_first: Check the vent valve and its filter for dirt, water or bugs, test its wiring, connector and fuse, and check the charcoal canister before replacing the valve or canister.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Vent Control Circuit Open
plain: The computer sees a break in the electrical circuit for the EVAP vent valve.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives
checks: Check the vent valve connector, which is often near the fuel tank and exposed to road dirt
Measure the vent valve resistance
fix: Usually a new vent valve or a wiring repair.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Vent Control Circuit Shorted
plain: The computer sees a short in the vent valve circuit, or the vent valve stays closed when it should be open.

causes.name: Wiring shorted to ground or power

checks: Measure the vent valve resistance
Check the vent valve and filter for blockage
fix: Usually a new vent valve or a wiring repair.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Vent Valve/Solenoid Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem with the EVAP vent valve, which sits near the fuel tank or charcoal canister.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Corroded connector at the vent valve

checks: Inspect the vent valve connector for corrosion and broken locks
Measure the solenoid resistance
Check for power and ground with the key on
fix: Usually a new vent valve or a connector repair.
examples: Frequently seen on GM trucks and SUVs, where the vent valve sits near the fuel tank
drive: Usually safe to keep driving. If the pump nozzle keeps clicking off, don't force extra fuel in. If you smell strong raw fuel or see fuel leaking, stop driving and get it checked right away because of the fire risk.
test_first: Check the fuse and the wiring and connector at the vent valve, measure the solenoid's resistance and confirm the computer's command before replacing the valve.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "C" Circuit
plain: The computer sees an electrical problem with a third EGR sensor, used on some engines (mostly diesels) to monitor EGR flow or position.
symptoms: EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the sensor reference voltage, ground and signal at the connector
Inspect wiring near hot exhaust parts
fix: Usually a new sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "C" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: EGR sensor "C" is giving readings that do not fit how the engine is running.
symptoms: EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the sensor reference voltage, ground and signal at the connector
Inspect wiring near hot exhaust parts
fix: Usually a new sensor; clean any clogged ports.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "C" Circuit Low
plain: The EGR sensor "C" signal is lower than possible.
symptoms: EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the sensor reference voltage, ground and signal at the connector
Inspect wiring near hot exhaust parts
fix: Replace the sensor or repair the shorted wiring.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "C" Circuit High
plain: The EGR sensor "C" signal is higher than possible, often from an open wire.
symptoms: EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the sensor reference voltage, ground and signal at the connector
Inspect wiring near hot exhaust parts
fix: Replace the sensor or repair the wiring.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "C" Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: The EGR sensor "C" signal keeps dropping out or jumping around.
symptoms: EGR may be shut off, raising emissions
checks: Check the sensor reference voltage, ground and signal at the connector
Inspect wiring near hot exhaust parts
fix: Repair the wiring or connector, or replace the sensor.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "A" Circuit High
plain: The control circuit for the valve that lets air pump air into the exhaust is reading higher voltage than expected, usually from an open wire or a bad valve.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Check the valve resistance and wiring
Inspect the connector for corrosion or water
fix: Usually a new switching valve or a wiring repair.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Pressure Sensor
plain: The computer sees a problem with the fuel tank pressure sensor, which it uses to check the fuel vapor system for leaks.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives
checks: Check the tank pressure reading with the gas cap off (should read near zero)
Inspect the sensor wiring and connector
fix: Usually a new fuel tank pressure sensor.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
plain: The fuel tank pressure sensor is giving readings that do not make sense, for example not reading zero with the gas cap off.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Overfilling the tank after the pump clicks off

checks: Check the pressure reading with the gas cap off
Inspect the vent valve and hoses for blockage
Stop topping off the tank when filling
fix: Usually a new fuel tank pressure sensor; fix any blocked vent first.
drive: Usually safe to keep driving. Stop filling when the pump clicks off rather than topping off. If you smell strong raw fuel or see a leak, stop driving and get it checked right away.
test_first: Compare the tank pressure sensor reading with the gas cap off, check the vent valve and hoses for blockage, and inspect the wiring before replacing the sensor.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Pressure Sensor Low Input
plain: The fuel tank pressure sensor signal is lower than it should be, usually from a sensor or wiring fault.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Blocked or kinked vent line causing vacuum in the tank

checks: Check the sensor reading with the gas cap off
Check reference voltage and ground at the sensor
Inspect wiring along the tank
fix: Usually a new fuel tank pressure sensor or a wiring repair.
drive: Usually safe to keep driving; this is an emissions-system fault that rarely changes how the car runs. Make sure the gas cap is on tight. If you smell strong raw fuel or see fuel leaking, stop driving and get it checked right away because of the fire risk.
test_first: Check the sensor's signal and reference voltage for a short to ground, inspect the connector, and check for a blocked vent line before replacing the sensor.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Pressure Sensor High Input
plain: The fuel tank pressure sensor signal is higher than it should be, usually from an open wire, a bad sensor or a blocked vent.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Blocked vent valve or vent hose

checks: Check the sensor reading with the gas cap off
Inspect the vent valve and filter for blockage
Check the sensor ground and wiring
fix: Usually a new fuel tank pressure sensor, or clearing a blocked vent.
drive: Usually safe to keep driving. If the pump nozzle keeps clicking off, don't force extra fuel in. If you smell strong raw fuel or see fuel leaking, stop driving and get it checked right away because of the fire risk.
test_first: Check the sensor's signal and ground wires for an open, inspect the connector, and make sure the vent valve and hose aren't blocked before replacing the sensor.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Pressure Sensor Intermittent
plain: The fuel tank pressure sensor signal is cutting in and out or jumping around.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives
checks: Wiggle the harness while watching the sensor reading
Inspect the connector for corrosion
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new sensor.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (large leak)
plain: The computer found a large leak in the system that stores fuel vapors, or no vapor flow at all. A missing or loose gas cap is the classic cause.
symptoms: Fuel smell around the car in some cases
No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Gas cap missing, loose or not sealing
Purge valve stuck closed or vent valve stuck open

checks: Check the gas cap first and make sure it clicks tight
Have a smoke test done to find the leak
Test the purge and vent valves
fix: Often a gas cap or a disconnected hose; otherwise a purge valve, vent valve or canister.

cost.job: Smoke test and repair EVAP leak

examples: A gas cap left loose after filling up is one of the most common triggers
drive: Check the gas cap first; a loose or missing cap is the most common cause. Usually safe to keep driving, but if you smell strong raw fuel or see fuel dripping, stop driving and get it checked right away because of the fire risk.
test_first: Check the gas cap, then smoke test the EVAP system to find the leak, and confirm the purge and vent valves seal before replacing the canister.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (very small leak)
plain: The computer found a very tiny leak in the fuel vapor system, smaller than a pinhole. It does not affect driving but it does let fuel vapor escape.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Gas cap seal worn or slightly loose
Small crack in an EVAP hose or fitting

checks: Replace the gas cap if the seal is old and clear the code
Have a smoke test done to find the leak
Test the purge and vent valves for leaking
fix: Often a gas cap, purge valve or vent valve; a smoke test finds the exact leak.

cost.job: Smoke test and repair EVAP leak

drive: Usually safe to keep driving; this is an emissions-system fault that rarely changes how the car runs. Make sure the gas cap is on tight. If you smell strong raw fuel or see fuel leaking, stop driving and get it checked right away because of the fire risk.
test_first: Inspect and test the gas cap seal, then smoke test the EVAP system to find the small leak before replacing the canister, valves or hoses.

title: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (fuel cap loose/off)
plain: The computer thinks the gas cap is loose or missing because it sees a big vapor leak right after refueling.
symptoms: Gas cap warning light on some vehicles
No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Gas cap left loose or off after fueling
Worn or damaged gas cap seal
Wrong or poor-quality replacement gas cap
EVAP leak elsewhere in the system

checks: Tighten the gas cap until it clicks
Inspect the cap seal and filler neck for damage
Replace the cap if it is old, then drive a few days to see if the light clears
fix: Usually just tightening or replacing the gas cap.
drive: Usually safe to keep driving. When you can, tighten the gas cap until it clicks; the light may go off after several drives. If you smell strong raw fuel or see a leak, stop driving and get it checked right away.
test_first: Inspect and test the gas cap and the filler neck sealing surface; if they're fine, smoke test the EVAP system before replacing other parts.

title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Low
plain: The circuit for the EVAP purge valve is reading lower voltage than it should, which usually means a short or a failed valve.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Open power feed or blown fuse

checks: Check for power at the purge valve connector
Measure the purge valve resistance
fix: Usually a new purge valve or a wiring repair.

title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit High
plain: The circuit for the EVAP purge valve is reading higher voltage than it should, often from an open circuit or failed valve.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives
checks: Measure the purge valve resistance
Inspect the connector and wiring
fix: Usually a new purge valve or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "B" Control Circuit
plain: On engines with a second EGR valve, the computer sees an electrical problem in the circuit that controls it.
checks: Command the EGR valve with a scan tool and compare actual position
Inspect the valve connector, wiring and the valve for carbon or soot
fix: Usually a new EGR valve "B" or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "B" Control Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The second EGR valve is not moving to the position the computer asks for.

causes.name: Carbon or soot making the valve stick

checks: Command the EGR valve with a scan tool and compare actual position
Inspect the valve connector, wiring and the valve for carbon or soot
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing EGR valve "B".

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "B" Control Circuit Low
plain: The control circuit for the second EGR valve is reading lower voltage than expected.
checks: Command the EGR valve with a scan tool and compare actual position
Inspect the valve connector, wiring and the valve for carbon or soot
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the valve.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "B" Control Circuit High
plain: The control circuit for the second EGR valve is reading higher voltage than expected, often from an open wire.
checks: Command the EGR valve with a scan tool and compare actual position
Inspect the valve connector, wiring and the valve for carbon or soot
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the valve.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "B" Control Stuck Open
plain: The computer thinks the second EGR valve is stuck open, which can make the engine run rough or lose power.
symptoms: Rough idle, stalling or lack of power

causes.name: Valve stuck open from carbon or soot

checks: Command the EGR valve with a scan tool and compare actual position
Inspect the valve connector, wiring and the valve for carbon or soot
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing EGR valve "B".

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "B" Control Stuck Closed
plain: The computer thinks the second EGR valve is stuck closed and cannot open when needed.

causes.name: Valve stuck closed from carbon or soot

checks: Command the EGR valve with a scan tool and compare actual position
Inspect the valve connector, wiring and the valve for carbon or soot
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing EGR valve "B".
